newsitem.title: USA: Ecuador's debts weaken on confusion over reform.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador's debts weaken on confusion over reform.

text.p: Ecuador's Brady bonds slipped in thin trading amid confusion over the course of the economic reform, market sources said.
The confusion apparently rose from tax measures in an economic package introduced by President Abdala Bucaram on Sunday.

Because the congress is in recess, those who oppose the measures demanded a full extraordinary session to vote on the plan, while Bucaram's party favors a speedier process, said Marco Santamaria, economist at ING Barings.
Hitting the snag affected only a small part of the plan, he said. The currency convertibility proposal -- the centerpiece of the package -- was not affected, he said.
Bucaram has threatened to hold a referendum if he fails to win congressional approval.

"I wouldn't be surprised that some elements of the plan will not be approved by Congress," said Alicia Duran, analyst at Merrill Lynch. But a referendum was fraught with danger for Bucaram at a time when his popularity appeared to be slipping. A year ago a constitutional amendment proposal put forth by Bucaram's predecessor was resoundingly defeated, she noted.
Ecuador Pars ECPARS=RR fell 5/8 to 47-1/4 bid.
Other Latin Braides tracked U.S. Treasuries lower after posting strong gains on Tuesday, but they managed to outperform on the retreat, traders said.
"There were no sellers," said a trader, noting the activity was slow compared with Tuesday.

Some of the most liquid issues, such as Brazil's C bond and Argentina's FRB, hit year-to-date high on Tuesday, which would normally invite profit-taking, but dealers were reluctant to trim their positions, said Marcelo Fleury, head of Brazil Desk at Garban Corp.
Dealers were also wary of shorting the market before the year-end, he said.
"It's hard to buy back in a thin market," he said.
The strong undertone recalled the last month of 1995 when the emerging market debts were at the peak and dealers were poised to add new positions in the new year, Marcelo said.
Argentina FRBs ARFLC05=RR slipped 3/8 to 86-5/8 bid and Brazil C BR8D14=RR eased 1/4 to 74.00 bid.
Bulgaria's Brady bond prices jumped in early European trading on hopes the introduction of a currency board would enable it to access the full annual International Monetary Fund limit loan.
"The prices (of Bulgaria's bonds) are strong on the screen," said a Brady trader. "But there were few trades.

The rally of Bulgarian Bradies was set against the bleak backdrop of a sinking currency and dwindling foreign currency reserves. The lev fell to a record low of 415-218 per dollar on Wednesday in the absence of central bank support.
Bulgaria FLRB BGFLIRG=RR rose 1-1/4 to 38-1/8 bid.
